title: Invariance-based methods rely on augmentations with strong biases
description: The paper states that invariance-based pretraining methods rely on hand-crafted data augmentations that introduce strong biases, may be detrimental for certain downstream tasks or different data distributions, and are not straightforward to generalize to other modalities like audio.
canonical_description: invariance-based methods rely on hand-crafted augmentations with strong biases limiting generalization

evidence.quote: they also introduce strong biases that may be detrimental for certain downstream tasks or even for pretraining tasks with different data distributions... Additionally, it is not straightforward to generalize these image-specific augmentations to other modalities such as audio.
